scoring_note: 45 objective points (1 each; item 11 counts as 5) + 20 production points (Writing 2 tasks and Speaking 2 tasks, rubric 0-5 each), converted to a weighted percentage. Achievement bands: 0-39 emerging, 40-59 developing, 60-79 consolidating, 80-100 B2 achieved.

items.stem: When is the delegation expected to arrive?
items.audio_text: Could you confirm exactly when the delegation is scheduled to arrive? — Of course. The full party is expected at approximately nine forty, and the transfer to the summit venue is fully guaranteed.

audios.text: I am pleased to open this session; could you provide a summary of your reasons?
I am reporting a theft; my briefcase was stolen outside the consulate.
It is highly probable that the keynote will be moved to the main auditorium.
Visitors are instructed to stay on the marked path; the wetland is strictly protected.
Under GDS rules, your cancellation fee might be waived once the account is cleared.

passages.reading_B: If our cooperative had not filed the complaint last month, the operator would have kept canceling our confirmed bookings. The account, which is now under compliance review, has been flagged, so no rebooking is possible until it is cleared. It is highly probable that the cancellation fees will be waived once the audit is complete. The delegation is likely to arrive at approximately nine forty; a revised schedule is being circulated. On the one hand the delay is frustrating; on the other hand, the review protects every member of the network.
passages.reading_C: Chair: I am pleased to (a)___ this meeting. Could you provide a (b)___ of your reasons for the 40% commission? — Delegate: Forgive me for (c)___, but we strongly (d)___ with that figure. — Chair: If I understand you correctly, you (e)___ that the commission should be reinvested locally.

writing.title: Formal complaint / claim letter to an OTA (120-160 words)
writing.prompt: Write a formal complaint letter to an international OTA. The cooperative's account has been blocked and the operator has been cancelling confirmed bookings. Explain the problem (present perfect / present perfect continuous), demand concrete actions assertively (I am writing to request..., we require that...) and ask for the cancellation fees to be waived (might be waived).
writing.rubric: formal and assertive register · present perfect (continuous) for the problem · clear and polite demands · correct technical terms (compliance / cancellation fees / waived) · cohesion, precision and spelling

writing.title: Choose ONE: (a) Chair's meeting summary OR (b) 'Colombia, a Mediator's Perspective' (120-160 words)
writing.prompt: (a) the chair's summary of a negotiation: opens the session, summarises positions, records the disagreement (we strongly disagree) and closes on time; or (b) the climate defence 'Colombia, a Mediator's Perspective': integrate advanced conditionals (If we had not integrated..., ... would be...) and compound passive (has been protected, would be closed).
writing.rubric: (a) meeting-minutes structure + chairing/negotiating language + closing; or (b) persuasive defence with advanced conditionals + compound passive + narration; cohesion and precision
writing.note: The student chooses one of two prompts; check whether the platform can model a choice.

speaking.title: Read aloud (40-55 s)
speaking.prompt: Read aloud your complaint letter from Writing Task 1 (or a description of the sustainable tourism symposium in London).
speaking.rubric: intelligible pronunciation · assertive and professional intonation · complete and fluent reading

speaking.title: Chair a negotiation (mini-pitch)
speaking.prompt: In the London executive room: open the meeting politely (I am pleased to open...), ask for a summary of reasons (Could you provide a summary...?), record a firm disagreement (we strongly disagree) and close on time. Then briefly defend the value of the destination with an advanced conditional.
speaking.rubric: chairs with the right formulas · handles disagreement firmly and tactfully · uses an advanced conditional in the defence · orderly closing · intelligibility
